## Solution

We solve $x'' + \lambda x = 0$ on $[a,b]$ with periodic boundary conditions $x(a)=x(b)$, $x'(a)=x'(b)$, $a<b$. Set $L = b-a > 0$.

**Case $\lambda > 0$.** Write $\lambda = \mu^2$, $\mu>0$. The general solution is
$$x(t)=A\cos(\mu t)+B\sin(\mu t),\qquad x'(t)=-A\mu\sin(\mu t)+B\mu\cos(\mu t).$$
The boundary conditions give the linear system in $A,B$:
$$A[\cos\mu a-\cos\mu b]+B[\sin\mu a-\sin\mu b]=0,$$
$$-A[\sin\mu a-\sin\mu b]+B[\cos\mu a-\cos\mu b]=0.$$
A nontrivial solution exists iff the determinant vanishes:
$$(\cos\mu a-\cos\mu b)^2+(\sin\mu a-\sin\mu b)^2=0.$$
This equals $|e^{i\mu a}-e^{i\mu b}|^2$, so it vanishes iff $e^{i\mu a}=e^{i\mu b}$, i.e.
$$\mu(b-a)=2n\pi,\qquad n\in\mathbb{Z}.$$
Since $\mu>0$, we get $\mu_n=\dfrac{2n\pi}{L}$, $n=1,2,3,\dots$, giving
$$\boxed{\lambda_n=\left(\frac{2n\pi}{b-a}\right)^2,\quad n=1,2,3,\dots}$$
When the determinant is zero, both equations collapse to $0=0$, so $A$ and $B$ are both free. The eigenspace is two-dimensional, spanned by
$$\cos\!\left(\frac{2n\pi\,t}{b-a}\right),\qquad \sin\!\left(\frac{2n\pi\,t}{b-a}\right).$$
Each positive eigenvalue has **multiplicity 2**.

**Case $\lambda = 0$.** The equation is $x''=0$, so $x(t)=A+Bt$. Then $x(a)=x(b)$ gives $B(b-a)=0$, hence $B=0$ (since $b\neq a$). The condition $x'(a)=x'(b)$ is then automatic. Thus
$$\boxed{\lambda_0=0,\quad x_0(t)=1\text{ (constant)},\text{ multiplicity }1.}$$

**Case $\lambda < 0$.** Write $\lambda=-\mu^2$, $\mu>0$. Then $x(t)=Ae^{\mu t}+Be^{-\mu t}$, $x'(t)=A\mu e^{\mu t}-B\mu e^{-\mu t}$. The boundary conditions yield
$$Ae^{\mu a}+Be^{-\mu a}=Ae^{\mu b}+Be^{-\mu b},\qquad Ae^{\mu a}-Be^{-\mu a}=Ae^{\mu b}-Be^{-\mu b}.$$
Adding: $A(e^{\mu a}-e^{\mu b})=0$. Since $a<b$ and $\mu>0$, $e^{\mu a}\neq e^{\mu b}$, so $A=0$. Subtracting: $B(e^{-\mu a}-e^{-\mu b})=0$, and $e^{-\mu a}\neq e^{-\mu b}$, so $B=0$. Only the trivial solution exists: **no negative eigenvalues**.

### Summary

The complete spectrum of the periodic boundary value problem $x''+\lambda x=0$, $x(a)=x(b)$, $x'(a)=x'(b)$ is:

- $\lambda_0 = 0$, with eigenfunction $x_0(t)=1$ (constant), multiplicity $1$;
- $\lambda_n = \left(\dfrac{2n\pi}{b-a}\right)^2$, $n=1,2,3,\dots$, with two linearly independent eigenfunctions
$$x_n^{(1)}(t)=\cos\!\left(\frac{2n\pi\,t}{b-a}\right),\qquad x_n^{(2)}(t)=\sin\!\left(\frac{2n\pi\,t}{b-a}\right),$$
each eigenvalue having multiplicity $2$.

There are no negative eigenvalues. Note the characteristic feature of the periodic problem: the eigenvalues are $\left(\frac{2n\pi}{L}\right)^2$ (period $L$, not $2L$ as in the separated Dirichlet/Neumann cases), and every nonzero eigenvalue is double, reflecting the two-dimensional translation-invariant solution space of the periodic problem.
